authority: Autonomous continuation authorized by the user; human approval remains unconfirmed.

policy.representation: Expected baseline bytes are independently materialized from the selected immutable Git tree, not inferred from the supplied index, status or working bytes.
policy.defaults: Use deterministic neutral LF defaults with automatic platform/user EOL conversion disabled. Honor transformations explicitly requested by versioned attributes, including Git's built-in text/EOL behavior. Other built-in transformations require actual qualification; otherwise reject them as unsupported rather than silently applying or ignoring them.
policy.configuration: The independent derivation uses only controlled configuration and the selected tree's versioned attributes. Do not inherit caller/local/system/global configuration, info/attributes, templates, hooks or ambient Git overrides. Object replacement must not redefine the selected immutable revision. Qualify the concrete Git commands and environment before implementing them.
policy.external_filters: Reject declared external filters before any materialization can execute them. Do not run clean/smudge programs to define equality. Do not implement a parallel partial Git-attributes interpreter.
policy.comparison: Compare the complete relevant path set, actual bytes, regular-file types and platform-representable modes against the independent materialization. Recollecting fresh fingerprints from a corrupted baseline must not make it valid. Caller assume-unchanged, skip-worktree or altered index state cannot define expected source content.
policy.modes: Preserve and compare executable distinctions on platforms that represent them. On Windows, record the Git-tree mode and explicit platform projection; do not claim ordinary worktree bits prove Git's executable distinction or actual Q4 execution.
policy.unsupported: Unqualified transformations, links, submodules, ambiguous paths and incomplete materialization cannot establish an immutable baseline. Report the concrete unsupported condition; no zero, shortened census or success-shaped fallback.
policy.usage: Use this same policy for configured CLI baseline creation and supplied-Context validation. Do not modify the supplied source, its index or ambient configuration. Head evidence must continue to match its separately observed current-source snapshot.
policy.binding: Bind the compiled policy semantics and qualified Git identity through the existing source/controller/tool evidence. No new public Context field is authorized unless qualification establishes a genuine missing binding that needs another explicit amendment.
policy.ownership: Expected trees and any private index/config/template files are uniquely owned temporary resources. Cleanup is limited to their exact owned paths.

required_controls: Original fresh assume-unchanged baseline corruption is rejected while the genuine no-cycle baseline remains accepted.
Skip-worktree and altered index controls cannot conceal a different baseline.
Versioned LF/CRLF behavior and platform-representable mode controls match the declared representation.
Ambient configuration, caller info/attributes and object replacement cannot alter expected immutable content.
A declared external filter is rejected without executing a sentinel program.
The normal CLI and common validator agree on accepted independently materialized baselines.
Original path-alias, builtin/frozen-mode, physical-alias and all-nine/incomplete regressions remain.
limits: This is a deterministic source-representation policy, not a sandbox, authenticated ownership, atomic filesystem lease, Q4 controller-execution proof or complete quality acceptance.
